## TRA Timeline

#### JV formation and TRA execution

- 2016-06-28: Agreement of Contribution and Sale signed; Exhibit C attaches form-of MCK TRA
- 2016-07-05: 8-K Item 1.01 files the Contribution Agreement and form-of TRA
- 2017-03-01: Change Healthcare JV closes; executed MCK TRA effective (executed instrument not in McKesson's CIK directory)

#### FY2019 renegotiation

- 2018-Q2 (FY2019): TRA renegotiated; $90M McKesson-side liability extinguished in exchange for an allocation of tax amortization (amendment instrument not filed under McKesson's CIK)

#### Early termination

- 2022-10-03: Change Healthcare acquired by UnitedHealth/Optum
- 2022-10: Change Healthcare exercises TRA early-termination right; McKesson receives $126M cash payment, recorded as a Q3 FY2023 gain in Other income, net

## Explanation

McKesson is the beneficiary side of one of two parallel TRAs created at the March 1, 2017 formation of the Change Healthcare JV (PF2 Newco LLC / Change Healthcare LLC) under which the JV agreed to pay 85% of cash tax savings from amortization of contributed-asset tax basis (Section 754-style step-up plus contributed-basis amortization) to the MCK TRA Parties; this is an asset-contribution / drop-down TRA pattern, with the JV as obligor and McKesson as beneficiary, rather than the typical Up-C structure. The only TRA documents on file in McKesson's CIK are the form-of exhibits to the 2016 Contribution Agreement; the executed instrument and any amendments live under Change Healthcare's CIK (0001651562). The TRA was renegotiated in fiscal Q2 2019 (extinguishing $90M of McKesson-side liability for an allocation of tax amortization) and was terminated by Change Healthcare under the contract's own early-termination provisions in October 2022, shortly after the UnitedHealth/Optum acquisition closed; McKesson received a $126M cash payment that it recorded as a Q3 FY2023 gain. The termination instrument is not filed under McKesson's CIK. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
